title: Separate packed-bitset validation from the timed resident kernel
finding: The packed CPU calibration labelled its repeated measurement as kernel time, but compose_packed_rows revalidated every packed row on every warmup and measured repetition. That O(row-count) Python validation was therefore charged to the resident bitset kernel even though a persistent CPU/GPU backend would validate admission once. Direct execute_bitset calls also accepted unbounded repeat and warmup counts even though ProbeCase already owned canonical bounds.

change.summary: Validate packed operands exactly once before warmup and timing, then call one private already-admitted kernel for every repetition. Preserve strict validation for direct compose_packed_rows callers. Report validation time separately and include it in the one-shot path while excluding it from resident-kernel timing. Reuse the existing CUDA probe repeat/warmup ceilings instead of defining another budget.

measurement_contract.one_shot: pack + validate + median resident kernel + canonicalize
measurement_contract.direct_api: compose_packed_rows remains fail-closed and validates type, sign and middle-row reachability on every direct call

focused_regressions: exact Boolean support and digest still match the stdlib CSR oracle
packed validation is invoked once per execute_bitset call rather than once per warmup/repeat
direct compose_packed_rows still rejects negative rows and missing middle rows
execute_bitset reuses the existing maximum repeat and warmup budgets

next_if_useful: Use the corrected resident-kernel and one-shot decomposition when comparing a real owner-machine CUDA run or a future Rust CPU bitset probe; do not compare CUDA only against the deliberately high-overhead stdlib CSR oracle.

branch_hygiene.note: Only the existing exp/tensor-kernel-contract-01 line was advanced. No branch was created, deleted, renamed, force-updated or moved into the archive history anchor.
